# CONFORMANCE FIXTURES: sibling recovery (rule 16). A broken subtree suppresses
# what DEPENDED on it — the judgments its ancestors would have made — never its
# SIBLINGS: every independent subtree still reports its own findings, so one
# error cannot hide another. Each pin below is the SECOND finding, the one the
# spine-aborting checker never reached.

== both sides of a sum report
expr nope1 + nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== both sides of a product report
expr nope1 * nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== both sides of a comparison report
expr nope1 == nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== both sides of a condition report
expr nope1 && nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== both sides of a coalesce report
expr nope1 ?? nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== both arms of a ternary report
env flag: bool = true
expr flag ? nope1 : nope2
error unknown name 'nope2'

== a failed condition still lets the arms speak
expr 1 ? nope1 : 2
error unknown name 'nope1'

== an index key above a broken value reports
expr nope1[nope2]
error unknown name 'nope2'

== a method argument above a broken value reports
expr nope1.round(nope2)
error unknown name 'nope2'

== a lambda body above a broken value reports
expr nope1.filter(v => v + nope2)
error unknown name 'nope2'

== a fold's start reports beside its broken body
expr [1, 2].reduce((acc, v) => acc + nope1, nope2)
error unknown name 'nope2'
